chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Claude Hopkins and early Thirties swing pianists
summary: Hopkins is called a light but effective stride pianist who deserved more exposure.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: But talking about Tatum, where we were... This is the early Thirties.
In this period the important thing was to swing, wasn't it.
Fats and Earl, and Duke and his band, and Claude Hopkins... Did you know Claude Hopkins?
Claude had a good little band, I thought.
He was a stride pianist. He came out of the Jelly Roll Morton type of school, I think, more or less.
Light, but he was very effective, you know. He had that power (?) stride, and it was very rhythmic --
and you could dance to it.
He made some solo albums not many years ago, and they were very good, but nobody much really appreciated it.
I didn't think Claude as a pianist got the exposure that he should have had.
